title: The same visible trump, an opposite target

feedback.title: Below target — overtrump the visible club
feedback.summary: North has already trumped with a low Club. You are below target and still need this trick, so beating that visible trump with your higher Club is the reviewed choice — the opposite of when the same evidence calls for undertrumping.
points: Supporting: North's four of Clubs is already on the table, trumping the Hearts West led. That fact alone does not say whether you should beat it or not.
Decisive: you are below target and still need this trick. Beating the visible trump is what taking a needed trick requires here.
This is not the same situation as play_target_protection_004, where the same kind of visible trump called for undertrumping instead — there South was exactly on target and did not want the trick.

feedback.title: Giving away a trick that was there to take
feedback.summary: The two of Diamonds is off-suit and non-trump; it cannot beat North's already-played trump, and discarding it gives up a trick you are below target and need.
points: You hold no Hearts, so both cards are legal, but only the higher Club can beat North's already-visible trump.
Below target with tricks still needed, passing on an available win does not reduce what is still required later.
The visible trump itself is not the reason to avoid this trick — it is only the reason a plain Diamond discard cannot win it.

author_notes: EC-055 checkpoint-3 coverage: second Mixed tactical reading scenario, using a different combination of already-supported signals from play_mixed_tactical_001. Decisive signal: South's target state (below target here, versus exactly on target in play_target_protection_004) determines whether overtrumping the same kind of already-visible opponent trump is correct or wrong. Supporting signal: the visible trump (card-tracking) itself only establishes what specific card is needed to win, not whether winning is wanted. Deliberately mirrors play_target_protection_004's mechanism (a trump already visible in the current trick) to make the contrast explicit: the same visible evidence produces the opposite correct action once the target state flips. No claim is made about any trick beyond this one.
